verses.1: You have appointed the month of Aviv. You have also celebrated Passover for Yahweh your God, because in the month of Aviv, Yahweh your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
verses.2: And you offered sacrifices of peace offerings to the LORD your God, both on the day and at the place that the LORD had chosen for his name to be remembered there.
verses.3: He shall not eat anything that is cooked for seven days. He shall only eat coarse bread, because in haste you left the land of Egypt, so that you may remember the day you left Egypt. For all the days of your life.
verses.4: And I will not see any of your flocks in all your fields for seven days. Nor will I eat from the meat that you offer in the evening on the first day, until tomorrow.
verses.5: You shall not offer the Passover in any of the gates of your city, which Jehovah your God has given you.
verses.6: For in that place where Jehovah your God has chosen to make His name known, you shall offer sacrifices at evening, when the sun sets, just as it is scheduled for you to leave Egypt.
verses.7: And you ate and drank in the place that Jehovah your God chose for you. Then you turned around in the morning and went back to your tent.
verses.8: For six days, you shall eat unleavened bread. But on the seventh day, you shall observe a day of rest for the LORD your God. You shall not do any work.
verses.9: Seven times will I recount to you from the beginning. At the very beginning, when Hermesh began, he started counting seven times.
verses.10: And you shall celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread for Yahweh your God, from the time when you begin to gather the grain that your Lord Yahweh has blessed you with.
verses.11: And you shall rejoice before Jehovah your God. You, your children, your wives, your servants, and your animals will also rejoice. And the Levites who are in your gates, as well as the Gibeathites, the Yaminites, and the Almonim who are in your midst, will also rejoice in the place that Jehovah your God chooses for them to dwell in.
verses.12: And you remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and you obeyed and carried out all these commandments.
verses.13: The Festival of Unleavened Bread will be observed for seven days, among those who are gathered together from your community and from your homes.
verses.14: And you shall rejoice in your festivals, you and your children and your servants and your animals, and the lambs and goats, and the wild animals, and the birds that are in your gates.
verses.15: For seven days, you shall celebrate the LORD your God in the place that the LORD chooses. For the LORD your God will bless you in all your coming and in all your works. Then you shall be happy.
verses.16: Six times a year, one shall remember all your memories of the face of Jehovah your God, at the places He has chosen for those festivals: during the festival of Unleavened Bread, during the festival of Harvest, and during the festival of Ingathering. But one shall not look upon the face of Jehovah with empty hands.
verses.17: A man who extends his hand as a blessing from Jehovah your God, who has given you this gift.
verses.18: Judges and rulers will be given to you in every city that Jehovah your God gives you for your rule. They will judge the people fairly.
verses.19: Do not follow unjust judgments. Do not recognize false appearances. And do not take bribes, for bribes will blind the eyes of the wise and distort the words of the righteous.
verses.20: Justice, justice! You must pursue it in order to live and inherit the land that Jehovah your God has given you.
verses.21: Do not harm yourself, for all the trees around the altar of Jehovah your God are meant for you to use.
verses.22: And do not make for yourself a position that Jehovah your God hates.
